speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; can you tell me how long these episodes have been occurring and what triggers them?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To narrow down the cause, did you experience any wheezing, chest tightness, or a sensation of breathlessness at the end of your breath during those episodes? Additionally, have you noticed any weight loss or night sweats since the initial illness 8 weeks ago?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Chronic Bronchitis or Post-viral Cough.
The 1-month duration of cough and shortness of breath following a recent upper respiratory infection (fever, sore throat, congestion) is highly characteristic of post-viral airway hyperresponsiveness. While asthma is a differential, the clear temporal relationship with the recent viral illness makes post-infectious etiology more likely. I will proceed to confirm this with a Chest X-Ray to rule out lingering pneumonia or structural changes.
